params.body:
Nightwatch #40, today at 13:06, while a dealer was duplicating a photo:

```
League\Flysystem\UnableToCheckDirectoryExistence
Unable to check existence for: 23024/stocklist_car_image_8.jpeg
  app/Jobs/ProcessImage.php:366  ->  Storage::disk('vehicles')->exists($baseName)
```

The job hung for thirty seconds and gave up.

## What the call really does

The stack names it: `exists()` goes through `Filesystem->has()` to **`AwsS3V3Adapter->directoryExists()`**. `Storage::exists()` means "as a file **or** as a directory", and that second half is a `ListObjectsV2` over the prefix. For one photo that is a directory listing, and it takes as long as the folder is big.

`fileExists()` asks the one question we ever mean, and costs a HEAD.

## Three times is a shape

- The showroom slides listed a folder per redrawn slide until that ran into a fifteen-second timeout on 21 September (R S2-7.16).
- The daily mail broke the same day on `exists()` with a null path, and the exception took the whole round with it, so no dealer got their mail (R B1-2.16).
- Today, the photo mill.

So this is about the form and not the incident: on this disk we ask for a file. All **31** calls on the `vehicles` disk are converted, across eleven files. Comments that mention the old form stay as they are, because that is the history and not code.

`TheBucketIsNotAskedForADirectoryTest` reads every PHP line in `app/`, skips comments, and fails on `exists(` or `missing(` on that disk. There is no fourth time.

## One existing test rewritten

`AnAfficheWithoutAPhotoStillPrintsTest` pinned the old call as a literal string. Its point is the `filled()` guard in front of it, because an empty path makes the bucket throw a `TypeError`; that point is unchanged and the assertion now holds it, rather than holding the method name.

## Honestly

I ran hundreds of `exists()` calls against that bucket myself this afternoon while working out the photo paths, all in the expensive form. The timestamps do not line up with this incident, but I cannot rule out that those scans warmed the bucket up.

Verified locally: 401 tests, 2.249 assertions across everything touching photos, images, mail, integrations, leases and orders, plus the rule-catalogue tests; `phpstan analyse` green on the whole project.
params.title: Asking the bucket for a file is a HEAD, not a listing
